cohort: A cohort of 10,000 children, with 5,000 born vaginally, 2,500 by planned cesarean section, and 2,500 by induced cesarean section.
finding: Children born via cesarean section had a significantly higher rate of sensory integration dysfunction compared to those born vaginally, with planned cesarean section showing a higher rate than induced cesarean section.
mod_finding: Sensory integration dysfunction was lower in births by vaginal delivery and induced cesarean section compared to planned cesarean section.
